subject: Runtime geography, subprocessors, and who is responsible for deletion
messages:
From: Eleanor Price <eleanor.price@blueharborhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Aug 2028 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Quick Qs on where requests are executed and deletion responsibility

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — BlueHarbor's platform team asked for a short write-up we can include in our security review. Two concise items: where are inference requests processed when the customer is based in the EU (edge/region fallback behavior), and which parties are responsible for deletion when retention TTLs are triggered (we need to map deletion responsibility for our DPO).

Specifically:
- If an EU customer pins a model and uses your Hosted API, can requests be guaranteed to stay in-region? If not, what are fallback rules?
- Which subprocessors may see request payloads in normal operation vs. in failover/overflow?
- When a retention policy triggers, who executes the deletion — Redwood, cloud provider, or a subprocessor (and can we get a short audit trail example)?

If you have a short diagram + a list of subprocessors by region that would be ideal.

Best,
Eleanor
Eleanor Price
Head of Platform Security, BlueHarbor Health
security@blueharborhealth.com

P.S. We may request additional evidence, but this will get us through pre-RFP checks.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eleanor Price <eleanor.price@blueharborhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Aug 2028 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests are executed and deletion responsibility

Hi Eleanor — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then we'll attach the appendix and a quick diagram. Marissa and Jonas are looped in for the evidence pack.

Short answers:
1) Regional execution guarantees: We offer region pinning for EU customers on Hosted and Dedicated. If you pin to an EU region (eu-west-1 / eu-central-1), runtime routing will prefer EU execution nodes. We cannot absolutely prevent transient egress in two narrow cases: (a) cold-start routing to a provisioning control plane node during an autoscale event (control signals only, payload does not leave region), and (b) explicit customer-configured cross-region routing (e.g., for multi-region HA). For normal traffic and default failover settings, inference payloads remain inside the pinned region.

2) Subprocessors by scenario:
- Normal operation (EU region): Customer requests are handled by Redwood runtime nodes provisioned in the EU (we run on GCP/CloudInstances EU regions and our EdgeRun caching nodes in Frankfurt/Amsterdam). Subprocessors that may touch request data (transit or caching) include: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) EU regions, EdgeRun Ltd. (edge prefix caching), and our telemetry partner (OpsTrace EU).
- Overflow/failover: If EU capacity is exhausted and your policy allows regional fallback, requests may be routed to our Dedicated burst capacity in us-west (AWS) or to a partner soft-fail region. In that path, additional subprocessors (AWS us-west region operators) may process transient data.

3) Deletion responsibility: Redwood owns and executes application-tier deletion for inference payloads and cached KV material. When a retention TTL triggers, Redwood's control plane issues deletion jobs to the runtime and cache layers; cloud providers or storage subprocessors are responsible only for the physical removal of objects under their platform contracts (they do not make deletion policy decisions). We provide an audit log showing the job id, timestamp, and affected resource ids (example attached).

I'll attach: (a) a regional subprocessors appendix, (b) a simple routing diagram, and (c) a sample audit excerpt that demonstrates the deletion job lifecycle. If you want canonical legal statements we can include the subprocessor contract excerpts under NDA.

Next steps: Are you OK with a short phone call Monday to walk the DPO through the audit example?

Thanks,
Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Aug 2028 14:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests are executed and deletion responsibility

Eleanor — attaching the appendix and a lightweight diagram per Rafael's note. Key details in the appendix (high level):
- Region pinning is honored at the routing layer; our router checks customer config, model compatibility, and regional capacity before selecting a host pool.
- Cache TTL vs. persistent logs: short-lived prefix/KV cache entries (used for speed) default to 24 hours and are owned/evicted by Redwood runtime; persistent telemetry and audit logs live in encrypted buckets with 90-day default retention (configurable).
- Subprocessor list (EU): GCP (compute/storage eu-central-1), EdgeRun Ltd. (edge caching Frankfurt), OpsTrace EU (telemetry).
- Overflow candidates: AWS us-west-2 (compute burst), PartnerCompute Ltd. (contracted partner pool).

Sample audit excerpt included shows a deletion job that ran on 2028-07-01T03:12:06Z with job_id DEL-20280701-99 and affected resource keys. That excerpt demonstrates the three steps: job creation (control plane), runtime purge, storage tombstone confirmation (provider).

Attachments: 2028-08-11-redwood-regional-subprocessors-appendix.pdf (subprocessor list + short contractual notes), 2028-08-11-routing-diagram.svg (simple ASCII map included below).

ASCII routing map (very small):
EU Customer -> EU Edge (Frankfurt) -> EU Runtime Pool (GCP eu-central-1)
   if capacity==low -> (fallback allowed) -> US Burst Pool (AWS us-west-2)

Let us know whether you want stricter no-fallback enforcement (we can gate routes to strictly deny cross-region failover at the cost of availability).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

1) For the audit example, can you include a redacted request-id that correlates across the control-plane job and the storage tombstone? They want to see the chain end-to-end (control job -> runtime ack -> storage tombstone).
2) We'll propose 'no-fallback' on the initial pilot. Can you confirm the availability SLA impact (percentile and expected cold-start times) if we pick strict no-fallback?

If you can add the single redacted example and an SLA delta note, we'll attach to the internal approval packet. Happy to hop on a 30-min call next week.
